info:
In Russian, the infinitive is the base form of a verb, and it is the form that is listed in dictionaries. The infinitive serves as the unconjugated, generic form of the verb and is used to express the general action or concept without specifying the subject, tense, or mood. The infinitive form of a verb typically ends in -ть, -чь, -ться, or -чься.

Here are some examples:

Regular Verbs:

говорить (govorit') - to speak
читать (chitat') - to read
писать (pisat') - to write
Reflexive Verbs:

улыбаться (ulybat'sya) - to smile (oneself)
мыться (myt'sya) - to wash (oneself)
Irregular Verbs:

быть (byt') - to be
есть (est') - to eat
The infinitive is used in various grammatical constructions, and it is also the form that is cited when giving a command or instruction. It is a key concept in Russian grammar and is the starting point for conjugating verbs into different tenses, aspects, and moods.

The infinitive form of a verb typically ends in -ть, -чь, -ться, or -чься.
